OBITUARY REFERENCES
MR. CHAIRMAN: Honourable Members, I refer with profound sorrow to the passing
away of Shri Sudhir Ranjan Mazumdar, a former Member of this House on the 4th of
January, 2009 at the age of 69 years.
Born at Gangra village in the Comilla District of Bangladesh in May 1939, Shri Mazumdar
had his education at M.G .M.H.S. School, Maharaj Bir Bikram College and Calcutta University.
A teacher and a social worker, Shri Mazumdar organised and participated in various
social service programmes during natural calamities, particularly in Bangladesh, during
the Indo-Pak War of 1970-71. He started his legislative career with the membership of the
Tripura Legislative Assembly, where he was a Member from 10.1.1983 to 5.2.1988, 5.2.1988
to 18.2.1992 and, again, from 14.3.2008 to 4.1.2009. At the time of his death, he was a sitting
Member of the Tripura Legislative Assembly. Shri Mazumdar served as the Chief Minister
of Tripura from 5.2.1988 to 18.2.1992, during that period, he took welfare measures and
promoted good governance in the State. Earlier, he had also served as the Leader of the
Opposition in the Tripura Legislative Assembly.
Shri Sudhir Ranjan Mazumdar represented the State of Tripura in this House from
April, 1992 to April, 1998.
In the passing away of Shri Sudhir Ranjan Mazumdar, the country has lost a
distinguished social worker, an able parliamentarian and an administrator.
We deeply mourn the passing away of Shri Sudhir Ranjan Mazumdar.
I request the Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a mark of respect
to the memory of the departed.
[Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute]
MR. CHAIRMAN: Secretary General will convey to the members of the bereaved
family our sense of profound sorrow and deep sympathy.
ORAL ANSWERS TO QUESTIONS
Satyam Computers Scam
*21. SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRASEKHAR: Will the Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether any significant headway has been made into the Satyam Computers
Scam;
(b) if so, the details thereof, indicating the extent of misappropriation of funds, the
period for which these irregularities have been going on;
(c) the extent of involvement of auditors and others in the Scam; and

[RAJYA SABHA]2
(d) the steps taken/proposed to be taken to ensure to detect other cases of profit
boosting and other corporate frauds?
THE MINISTER OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS (SHRI PREM CHAND GUPTA): (a) to (d):
A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
Statement
(a) to (c) The Government has ordered investigation on 13.1.2009 under Sec. 235 of the
Companies Act, 1956 into the affairs of M/s Satyam Computer Services Ltd. to be carried
out by Inspectors drawn from the office of Serious Fraud Investigation Office. In addition,
the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India is also examining the role and the conduct
of the statutory auditors of the Company with regard to the statutory functions required
to be discharged by them. The said investigations and enquiries are currently under
progress.
(d) Under the framework provided by the Companies Act, 1956, all companies are
required to make statutory disclosures that reflect true and fair view of the state of affairs
of the company. To facilitate making of such disclosures by companies and for easy
viewing of the same by the stakeholders of the companies, general public and regulatory
agencies, Government has set up an electronic registry with round - the - clock access
through internet. Legal action is taken against such companies that do not comply with
the requirement. In addition, the Act provides for appointment of independent, statutory
auditors to audit the accounts and report to the shareholders. Such audited accounts are
also displayed on the electronic registry for general viewing. While the reporting
requirements are regulated under the Companies Act, 1956, the conduct of auditors is
regulated under the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949. In addition, for listed companies,
compliance with these statutory requirements is required to be certified by a company
secretary in practice, who in turn is regulated under the Company Secretaries Act, 1980.
The Act also provides powers to the Government to undertake inspection/ investigation
of companies and for prosecution for false statements relating to the Company in the
prospectus, the financial statements or otherwise. Subject to approvals by Company Law
Board, the Government can also take action against mismanagement and oppression in
companies by effecting changes in the management of the companies. Companies as are
listed on stock exchanges are also subject to regulation by Securities and Exchange Board
of India (SEBI) Act, 1992. The Government and various regulatory agencies take appropriate
action under the Companies Act, 1956 and other laws, as warranted, to detect and deal
with cases of falsehoods or corporate fraud, as the case may be, through the application
of the existing statutory framework.

finance companies or banking companies, they have to approach the Reserve Bank of

statutory auditors. The Reserve Bank of India has no legal power to blacklist any audit
firm. That is the job of the Institute of Chartered Accountants, and in fact, they also
cannot blacklist. They can issue an advisory. The Reserve Bank of India can issue an
advisory that the auditors of this firm, the partners of this firm have been found guilty of
some misconduct, and therefore, this company or this firm may not be engaged for the
audit work of a particular bank or a ccompany. So, this is the situation. With regard to the
accounts of the Global Trust Bank for 2002-03, certain deficiencies were noticed, and
therefore, the Reserve Bank of India had issued some sort of an advisory to banks and
NBFCs in October 2004 not to engage the Pricewaterhouse. After 3 years, that is, in
August 2007, Pricewaterhouse approached the Reserve Bank of India to consider allowing
them to carry on with the auditor work, and that is how the RBI, in their wisdom, thought
that this punishment of 3 years is good enough and they lifted the ban.

Establishment of museums at district and regional level
*22. MS. MABEL REBELLO:
SHRI B. J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to establish more museums at district and regional levels
to take the museum movement to the people in the country;
Written Answers to Starred Questions

[RAJYA SABHA]18
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also proposed to redefine the museum concept to keep pace with the
evolving social changes;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) what are the details of districts/regions where this new concept is proposed to be
implemented in Orissa and Jharkhand?
THE MINISTER OF CULTURE (SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI): (a) to (d) In order to
strengthen the museum movement and to re-invigorate the existing museum scenario in
the country the scheme for financial assistance for "Promotion and Strengthening of
Regional and Local Museums" was revised by Government in September, 2008. The salient
features of the revised scheme are as under:-
i. Financial assistance upto Rs. 6 crores for setting up of a Museum under Category-I
(State Museums and other Museums with exquisite collections) and upto Rs. 3 crores
for setting up a Museums under Category-II (Regional and Local Museums).
ii. Financial Assistance to existing museums for upgradation and modernization was
enhanced from Rs. 1.70 Crore to Rs. 5.00 crores in respect of Category-I Museums and
from Rs. 60.00 lakhs to Rs. 2.5 crores in respect of Category-II Museums.
iii. The scheme envisages financing by Government of India upto 80% of the estimated
amount (90% in case of museums in NE regions)
iv. Training and refresher courses for the museum staff are included as an integral part of
the Scheme.
v. Purchase of exhibits is not financed under the Scheme.
(e) The scheme is applicable to all eligible museums from all States, including Orissa
and Jharkhand.
Transportation of oil from caspian region
*23. SHRIMATI VIPLOVE THAKUR: Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether the issue of transportation of oil from Caspian region through the
Mediterranean and Red Sea into India was discussed during the visit of Foreign Minister
of Turkey to India in February, 2008;
(b) if so, the salient features of the discussion;
(c) whether it is also a fact that oil, if brought from Caspian region through the
Mediterranean and Red Sea, will be cheaper;
(d) if so, whether Government has taken any decision on the issue; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
THE MINISTER OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS (SHRI MURLI DEORA): (a)
and (b) The Foreign Minister of Turkey, during his visit to India in February 2008, had
Written Answers to Starred Questions

[17 FEBRUARY , 2009] 19
outlined a proposal for cooperation between Turkey, Israel and India for transportation of
crude oil from the Caspian region through the Mediterranean and Red Sea and into India.
Briefly, this project envisages transport of crude oil from Ceyhan port in Turkey to Ashkelon
port in Israel in the Mediterranean Sea, initially through Very Large Crude Carriers (VLCCs)
and eventually by laying a sub-sea pipeline. Thereafter, crude oil will be transported
through the existing Ashkelon -Eilat pipeline in Israel to Eilat port on the Red Sea. From
there, crude oil may be carried to India/other parts of Asia. The project is still in a conceptual
stage and requires a detailed feasibility study to establish its techno-commercial viability.
A tripartite meeting between Turkey-Israel-India was held in September 2008 at Ankara to
discuss conceptual features of the project.

(b) whether oil demand declined by 47 trillion barrel per day (tb/d) in October, 2008
following the highest figure of plus 200 tb/d of the year in September, 2008;

Black marketing of LPG cylinders in Delhi
179. MS. MABEL REBELLO:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL/GAS be pleased to state:

(b) whether some raids were conducted by Government to assess the enormity of
this menace; and
Written Answers to Unstarred Questions

[17 FEBRUARY , 2009] 87
(c) if so, the details thereof, inter-alia indicating the action plan of Government to
effectively control this menace?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL
GAS (SHRI DINSHA PATEL): (a) to (c) The possibility of blackmarketing/ diversion of
subsidized domestic LPG cylinders by some unscrupulous elements cannot be ruled out
due to the wide gap between the retail price of LPG for domestic use and the market price
for commercial LPG.
OMCs have detected 16 cases of diversion of LPG by their LPG distributorship in the
NCT of Delhi during the period April, 2008 to December, 2008. Action against the erring
distributors was taken as per provisions of Marketing Discipline Guidelines (MDG)/
Distributorship Agreement.
In order to stop blackmarketing/ diversion of domestic LPG cylinders, the Government
has enacted "Liquefied Petroleum Gas (Regulation of Supply and Distribution) Order,
2000" and formulated "Marketing Discipline Guidelines, 2001" which provides for penal
action against LPG distributors indulging in diversion/ blackmarketing of LPG .
Whenever OMCs receive complaints, these are investigated and if the /complaint is
established, suitable action is taken against the LPG distributor(s) in /accordance with the
provisions of the Marketing Discipline Guidelines (MDG). MDG provides for following
action against the distributor:-
– Fine of Rs. 20,000 plus the price of LPG diverted at commercial rates for 1st offence.
– Fine of Rs. 50,000 plus the price of LPG diverted at commercial rates for 2nd offence.
– Termination of the distributorship for 3rd offence.
In addition to the action taken by the OMCs, State Governments are empowered under
the LPG (Regulation of Supply & Distribution) Order, 2000 promulgated under the Essential
Commodities Act, 1955 to take action against blackmarketing/diversion of domestic LPG .
Similarly, the Weights and Measures Departments of the States / UTs initiate legal action
against those LPG distributors found blackmarketing/diversion of LPG cylinders. The
State Governments have been alerted from time to time to take steps against the
biackmarketing/diversion of domestic cylinders for unauthorized usage.
Government have issued advertisements cautioning the public that use of domestic
LPG for non-domestic purposes is illegal, dangerous and against national interest. Through
these advertisements, cooperation of the general public has also been sought to report
any irregularity / malpractice to the OMCs.
The officials of OMCs carry out random checks at distributors godowns, delivery
points, as well as en-route to ensure that no misuse takes place. The distributors of OMCs
are under strict instructions to check the weight of cylinders at their godowns before
delivery, and only cylinders with the specified weight are to be delivered to the customers.
The distributors have also been instructed to ensure that the seals are verified & shown
to the customers at the time of delivery. In case any under-weight cylinder is received by
the customer, such cylinders are replaced free of charge by the OMCs.
OMCs have introduced different colours for domestic and non-domestic LPG cylinders
for controlling the diversion of domestic LPG for unauthorized use.

Technology upgradation of refineries
†190.SHRI RAJ MOHINDER SINGH MAJITHA:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR JOSHI:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that on an average 28 to 29 litres of petrol and 85 litres of diesel
are yielded by processing of one barrel of crude oil in crude oil processing industries of
the country;
(b) if not, the details thereof and the average production of petrol and diesel from
processing of one barrel of crude oil in oil refineries of the country;
(c) whether this average can be increased by technology upgradation; and
(d) if so, the reaction of Government in this regard?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL
GAS (SHRI DINSHA PATEL): (a) and (b) The average production of petrol and diesel in
India varies from refinery to refinery depending upon the configuration and type of crude
oil processed. Most of the inland refineries in India were established based on low sulphur
indigenous crude oil processing whereas the coastal refineries predominantly process
high sulphur imported crude oil. The average yield in the country is only 17 litres of petrol
and 65 litres of diesel.
(c) and (d) Yes, Sir. The average yield can be increased to certain extent through
selective crude oil processing and substantially through improved secondary processing,
i.e. technology upgradation and improved configuration. The oil Public Sector Undertakings
have continuously implemented projects to increase refining capacity and maximization of
distillates in order to achieve self-sufficiency in petroleum products in the country. Fluidized
Catalytic Cracking, Hydrocracking, Hydrotreaters, Delayed Cokers, Catalytic Reformers,
Isomerization, Alkylation Units etc. have been selectively added in the refineries for
maximization of distillate yield including petrol and diesel.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL

and Island territories) and optional blending of 10% ethanol with petrol from October 2007

pilot projects have been undertaken at two locations at Aonla Depot in U.P. and  Desur
Depot in Karnataka from 15.12.2008 and 20.12.2008 respectively. The pilot study is likely to
be completed by 30.6.2009.

Fixation of sale price of petrol and diesel
†209.SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
SHRI SHIV ANAND TIWARI:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the rate of consumer sale prices of petrol and diesel in the
country is fixed on the basis of trade parity pricing system;
(b) if so, the details of expenditure regarding the product being factored under the
above system;
(c) the reasons for adaptation of above system instead of common basis of production
cost to fix the consumer sale price; and
(d) the differences and characteristics of above said both systems?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL
GAS (SHRI DINSHA PA TEL): (a) and (b) Based on the Rangarajan Committee's
recommendations, effective 16 June 2006, Government approved the refinery gate pricing
of Petrol and Diesel on Trade Parity basis, which is the weighted average of Import Parity
and Export Parity prices, in the ratio of 80:20. The build up of retail selling price of Petrol
and Diesel includes the following elements:
(i) Price paid to refinery on Trade Parity basis.
(ii) Inland freight up to the market
(iii) Marketing Margin
(iv) Dealer Commission
(v) Excise duty
(vi) V alue Added tax and local levies
(c) and (d) As the country imports more than 75% of its crude oil requirements, domestic
prices of petroleum products are, to a very large extent, influenced by international oil
prices. Hence, the adoption of Trade Parity pricing for Petrol and Diesel. In petroleum
refining, crude oil is processed through numerous processing streams. The blending of
intermediate product streams from various processing units for making finished petroleum
products makes its difficult to apportion the total cost to individual refined products with
reasonable accuracy. Therefore, individual product-wise costs are not identified separately.
The Government dismantled Administered Pricing Mechanism (APM) w.e.f. 1st April,
2002, which was based on the cost plus methodology for determining prices of petroleum
products. The APM had the following disadvantages:
(1) APM: did not provide strong incentives for investments in technological upgradations
or for cost minimization.

(2) There was no incentive for oil companies to generate internal resources for making
investments for the future.
(3) Private capital as well as foreign direct investment would not be forthcoming in view
of the regulatory controls inherent in the APM.
(4) Subsidies and cross-subsidies resulted in wide distortions in the consumer prices
and did not reflect the economic cost of petroleum products.
The Government's decision to determine domestic prices of petroleum products on the
basis of international prices is intended to make the oil companies globally competitive, to
attract investments in petroleum sector to meet the growing demand, and to promote
efficiency and better customer service through competition.

Water Requirement of increasing population
241. SHRI MOHD. ALI KHAN: Will the Minister of W ATER RESOURCES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether population of the country is expected to 140 crore by 2025; and
(b) if so, the steps being taken to give water to each State to meet the population
requirements in each State especially in Andhra Pradesh?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF W ATER RESOURCES (SHRI JAI
PRAKASH NARAYAN YADA V): (a) As per report of Technical Group on Population
Projection constituted by National Commission on Population, the projection of the
population of country is 139 crore by 2025.
(b) Various steps for planning and implementation of water resources projects for
meeting the projected requirement of water for different purposes are taken by the
respective State Governments. Government of Andhra Pradesh have informed that several
activities related to development of water resources have been taken up under
"Jalayagnam".
Ministry of Water Resources provides central assistance under its various programmes
to all States including Andhra Pradesh. Due emphasis has been laid on development and
management of water resources projects during the XI Plan. An outlay of Rs. 2,32,311
crore has been provided for the irrigation, command area development  and  water
management and flood control in the XI Plan against the X Plan outlay of Rs.95,743 crore.

Dismay over Disinvestment of PSU  Shares
SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN (West Bengal) : Sir, I rise to express my concern
over the renewed move of the Government to start disinvestment in the profitable
public sector. Only one day before, in Lok Sabha, and also in this House, while
commending the Budget, the hon. Finance Minister spoke quite high of the role of
the public sector in stabilising and protecting the national economy, in the background
of the severe global financial crisis. But, immediately after that commendment made in
Budget, on the next day, as reported by the Press, the Government is again planning
to offload shares of the profitable public sector in the market. That is totally against
the national interest and particularly so, when the stock market is sinking.
The prices are going down, and at this time, this renewed initiative to sell out
the shares of the profitable public sector means handing over the control of the public

sector units to private hands at throw away prices because now the prices are sinking,
and this is all the more dangerous particularly when the public sector companies are
also having different other routes to raise money through bonds and debentures, and
in the changed financial circumstances, common people are having more faith on the
bonds and debentures issued by the public sector. So, it is not just necessary that
the equity route has to be adopted by the public sector to raise funds. So, from all
logic, this is completely illogical proposition to go in for offloading shares of the public
sector, and through you, Sir, I urge upon the Government not to resort to such a
dangerous exercise which will finally mean a total fraud of a different type on the
national economy and the people of the country.

STATEMENT BY MINISTER
Regarding Alleged Misbehaviour of Police in Jharkhand
THE MINISTER OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM) : This morning,
hon. Member Shri Yashwant Sinha and certain other hon. Members made submissions
on the incidents that took place at the gates of the Raj Bhawan in Ranchi, Jharkhand
on February 12, 2009. I have been briefed on the submissions and I am distressed
that such an incidents should have taken place on that day.
The Government of India has received information from the State Government. The
DGP, Jharkhand has also report.
It is reported that prominent leaders of the BJP, along with a few thousands
workers, marched towards the several gates of the Raj Bhawan. At gate no. 3, the
demonstrators were led by two MLAs; they demonstrated peacefully behind the
barricade; and there was no incident. At gate no. 4 the demonstrators were ley by an
MLA; they also demonstrated peacefully behind the barricade and there was on
incident.
The incident occurred between gate no. 2 and no.1 which is the main gate. It is
reported that the demonstrators were led by Shri Yashwant Sinha, M.P., Shri Arjun
Munda, MLA, Shri Saryu Rai, MLA, Shri Dinesh Sarangi, MLA, Shri Loknath Mahto,
Statement by Minister

[RAJYA SABHA]212
MLA and Shri Raghubar Das, MLA and States President, BJP. Announcements were
made over the public address system that orders under Section 144, Cr. P.C. had been
promulgated in that area. Notwithstanding the announcement, the demonstrators broke
the barricade and moved towards gate no. 2. Thereafter, ignoring repeated
announcements over the public address system that the assembly had become unlawful
and that the demonstrators should disperse, the demonstrators broke the second
barricade outside gate no. 2 nad proceeded towards gate no. 1.
In roder to contain the agitators, the police used a water cannon. When that failed
to deter the agitators, the police had no option but to resort to a mild lathi charge.
According to the report submitted by the Director-General of Police, Shri Yashwant
Sinha, Shri Arjun Munda and Shri Saryu Rai, besides some others, sustained injuries.
I have with me the injury reports, but since Shri Yashwant Sinha himself has stated
before the House that he was not complaining about the injuries, it may not be
necessary to refer to the injury reports. However, I may add that the Circle Officer,
Namkum, Shri Amit Kumar personally accompanied Shri Yashwant Sinha to the Seva
Sadan Hospital where he was treated. Shri Arjun Munda and Shri Saryu Rai were taken
by the officers of the District Administration to Adre House, where the doctors
attached to Raj Bhawan administered first aid to them. Shri Yashwant Sinha and the
two MLAs were arrested at about 1430 hours and were released at about Shri
Yashwant Sinha has referred to certain persons who were injured. We have gathered
the facts. The DGP, Jharkhand has reported that Shri Ram Jatan Paswan, PSO, suffered
an abrasion on te left knee which was a simple injury. A police constable by name
Shri Prakash Kumar suffered a lacerated wound on the left side of the scalp, which
was also a simple injury. We have not been able to gather any information about the
injuries to Shri Himanshu, Private Secretary to Shri Yashwant Sinha, since the police
have not been able to locate ay injury report in that case. If Shri Yashwant Sinha
would be kind enough to share with me more information about the hospital or doctor
who treated Shri Himanshu, I shall endeavour to gather more information.
According to the records the Nagarmal Modi Seva Sadan Hospital, 89
demonstrators were registered as patients, out of which two had suffered fractures on
the leg and one had suffered a head injury. They were admitted to the hospital and
subsequently discharged. The district administration has reported that 15 police
personnel also sustained minor injuries due to stone pelting and use of sticks by the
demonstrators.
DGP, Jharkhand has reported that 300 demonstrators were detained adn released
later in the evening.
DGP, Jharkhand has also reported that the district administration had, by a fax
message, informed the Secretary General, Rajya Sabha and the Speaker of the State
Legislative Assembly without any delay on the same evening, that is, February 12,
2009 about the arrest and release of the Members of the respective Houses. However,
on being advised that the message in respect of Shri Yashwant Sinha should have
been addressed to the Hon’ble Chairman, Rajya Sabha, another fax message was sent
on February 13, 2009 to the Hon’ble Chairman, Rajya Sabha.
Statement by Minister

[17 FEBRUARY , 2009] 213
Mr. Vice-Chairman, I am distressed and unhappy that such an incident should have
taken place. I have placed the facts before the House. I have great respect for hon.
Members who have complained about the alleged police excess, but I am not able to
make any judgement in this behalf. I offer my sympathies to those who have suffered
injuries. I wish that such demonstrations are conducted peacefully and no cause is
given for any action by the police.

me an opportunity to place our views on the Motion of Thanks on the President's Address.
The President's Address is a compliation of the functioning of the UPA Government
during the last five years. It is nothing but a jugglery of statistics and date collection. Sir,
I would like to focus on there major issues with reference to this President's Address,
namely, the Sri Lankan Tamil issue, the functioning of the telecommunications and the
spectrum scandal and the UPA Government's handling of terrorism during its tenure.
Sir, the plight of innocent Tamil civilians of Sri Lanka is a serious concern. The on-
going war between the Government of Sri Lanka and the LTTE has resulted in a humanitarian
disaster, including massive civilian casualties and the internal displacemtn of nearly 250,000
innocent civilians. Under the guise of war, the Sir Lankan Government  has been creating
a humanitarian crisis of a gargantuan proportion by systematically cleansing the Tamil
ethnicity. It is a clear genocide of Tamils. Lakhs of Tamil people in Mullaitheevu are
suffering without any food or medicine, facing annihilation due to indiscirminate shelling
